```text
354	static void cv_marvin_v1_task(void *param)
355	{
356	    (void)param;
357	
358	    QueueHandle_t frames = xQueueCreateStatic(CV_FRAME_QUEUE_DEPTH,
359	                                              sizeof(Video_FrameInfo),
360	                                              s_frame_queue_storage,
361	                                              &s_frame_queue_buf);
362	    configASSERT(frames != NULL);
363	    bool subscribed = Video_SubscribeFrames(frames);
364	    configASSERT(subscribed);
365	
366	    QueueHandle_t bus = Detector_BusQueue();
367	    configASSERT(bus != NULL);
368	
369	    LOG_INFO("CV: cv_marvin_v1 started\r\n");
370	
371	    publish_detector_config();
372	
373	    for (;;)
374	    {
375	        Video_FrameInfo frame;
376	        if (xQueueReceive(frames, &frame, portMAX_DELAY) != pdTRUE) { continue; }
377	
378	        /* Always drain, even when disabled, so frames don't back up. */
379	        if (!Detector_IsEnabled(DETECTOR_CV_MARVIN_V1)) { continue; }
380	        if (frame.buffer == NULL)                       { continue; }
381	        if (frame.width == 0u || frame.height == 0u)    { continue; }
382	        if (frame.bytes_per_pixel != CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL){ continue; }
383	
384	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_START, frame.frame_count, 0u);
385	        detect_frame(&frame, bus);
386	        PerfLog_EmitStamp(PERF_STAGE_CV_END, frame.frame_count, 0u);
387	
388	        /* Re-emit detector config at ~1 Hz so a mid-stream host attach
389	         * picks it up within a second of frames flowing. Cheap (~188 B/s
390	         * × 1 record/s). When config becomes runtime-tunable, this becomes
391	         * the heartbeat — on-change emits land via publish_detector_config
392	         * directly from the setter path. */
393	        if ((frame.frame_count % 60u) == 0u) { publish_detector_config(); }
394	
395	        /* Sensing strip centers on the sensor row (y=311); strike strip is
396	         * below the sensors at the strum trigger zone. Both pre-overlay so
397	         * the host viewer sees the same pixels the detector consumed. */
398	        const uint32_t fstride = (uint32_t)frame.width * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
399	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_SENSING,
400	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
401	                                   265u, 300, 185u, 32u);
402	        PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(frame.frame_count, PERF_STRIP_STRIKE,
403	                                   (const uint8_t *)frame.buffer, fstride,
404	                                   212u, 395u, 290u, 32u);
405	
406	        draw_overlay((uint8_t *)frame.buffer, frame.width, frame.height);
407	
408	        // /* ~2 Hz signal dump for threshold tuning. hold/edge values shown
409	        //  * vs the 50 threshold, with P/E flags reflecting current state. */
410	        // if ((frame.frame_count % 30u) == 0u)

412	        //     LOG_INFO("CV: G %3d/%3d%c%c R %3d/%3d%c%c Y %3d/%3d%c%c B %3d/%3d%c%c O %3d/%3d%c%c\r\n",
```

```text
169	}
170	
171	/* Hide HEO and let BASE (Legato UI) fill the whole panel. */
172	static void lcd_unbind(void)
173	{
174	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, false, true);
175	    XLCDC_REGS->LCDC_BASECFG4 &= ~LCDC_BASECFG4_DISCEN_Msk;
176	    XLCDC_SetLayerEnable(XLCDC_LAYER_BASE, true, true);
177	}
178	
179	/* ─── Frame-done ISR (runs in IRQ context) ─────────────────────────────── */
180	
181	static void on_frame_done(uint32_t frame_count,
182	                          uint32_t buffer_addr,
183	                          uintptr_t ctx)
184	{
185	    (void)ctx;
186	
187	    BaseType_t higher_priority_task_woken = pdFALSE;
188	    PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_ISC_IRQ, frame_count, 0u,
189	                             &higher_priority_task_woken);
190	
191	    s_latest_buffer = buffer_addr;
192	
193	    /* Re-point HEO at the buffer that was just completed so the panel sees
194	     * every captured frame. With the descriptor ring and a static base
195	     * binding, HEO would only see frames written to slot 0. The address
196	     * latches at next vsync (XLCDC update=true); HEO and ISC run on
197	     * independent clocks so this is fine. Skip when display is hidden. */
198	    if (s_display_bound)
199	    {
200	        XLCDC_SetLayerAddress(XLCDC_LAYER_HEO, buffer_addr, true);
201	    }
202	
203	    Video_FrameInfo info =
204	    {
205	        .buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)buffer_addr,
206	        .frame_count     = frame_count,
207	        .width           = s_src_w,
208	        .height          = s_src_h,
209	        .bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL,
210	    };
211	
212	    uint32_t subscriber_mask = 0u;
213	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
214	    {
215	        QueueHandle_t q = s_subscribers[i];
216	        if (q != NULL)
217	        {
218	            (void)xQueueSendFromISR(q, &info, &higher_priority_task_woken);
219	            subscriber_mask |= (1u << i);
220	        }
221	    }
222	    PerfLog_EmitStampFromISR(PERF_STAGE_VIDEO_PUBLISH, frame_count,
223	                             subscriber_mask, &higher_priority_task_woken);
224	    portYIELD_FROM_ISR(higher_priority_task_woken);
225	}
226	
227	/* ─── Capture state machine ────────────────────────────────────────────── */
228	
229	static bool capture_arm(void)
230	{
231	    uint16_t w = 0, h = 0;
232	    if (!TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)) { return false; }
233	
234	    if (!ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)) { return false; }
235	    s_src_w = w;
236	    s_src_h = h;
237	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(true);
238	    if (!ISC_Capture_Start())
239	    {
240	        (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
241	        return false;
242	    }
243	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture ARMED %ux%u\r\n", w, h);
244	    return true;
245	}
246	
247	static void capture_disarm(void)
248	{
249	    ISC_Capture_Stop();
250	    (void)TC358743_EnableStream(false);
251	    LOG_INFO("VIDEO: capture IDLE\r\n");
252	}
253	
254	/* Bind/unbind display from current intent + most-recent source size +
255	 * caller-set window. A zero-sized window means the app hasn't set one
256	 * yet — silently skip the bind in that case rather than emit a malformed
257	 * HEO geometry; DisplayShow without a prior SetWindow is a no-op. */
258	static void display_apply(void)
259	{
260	    window_t w = s_window;
261	    bool window_valid = (w.w != 0u) && (w.h != 0u);
262	    bool source_valid = (s_src_w != 0u) && (s_src_h != 0u);
263	    bool want = s_display_shown && source_valid && window_valid;
264	
265	    if (want && !s_display_bound)
266	    {
267	        lcd_bind(s_src_w, s_src_h, w.x, w.y, w.w, w.h);
268	        s_display_bound = true;
269	    }
270	    else if (!want && s_display_bound)
271	    {
272	        lcd_unbind();
273	        s_display_bound = false;
274	    }
275	}
276	
277	/* Each tick: align current chain state (capture armed / display bound) to
278	 * the user's intent flags, given the current source-lock state. */
279	static void reconcile(void)
280	{
281	    bool locked = TC358743_IsLocked();
282	
283	    /* Capture: armed iff intent + lock. */
284	    bool want_capture = s_capture_enabled && locked;
285	    if (want_capture && !s_capture_armed)
286	    {
287	        if (capture_arm()) { s_capture_armed = true; }
288	    }
289	    else if (!want_capture && s_capture_armed)
290	    {
291	        capture_disarm();
292	        s_capture_armed = false;
293	    }
294	
295	    /* Display: shown iff intent + we have a source size to work with. The
296	     * source size is captured at arm time and persists across capture
297	     * teardown so the user can leave HEO bound on a stale frame. */
298	    display_apply();
299	}
300	
301	/* ─── Task body ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
302	
303	static void video_task(void *param)
304	{
305	    (void)param;
306	
307	    /* One-time init in task context (scheduler running, so synchronous I²C
308	     * and SYS_TIME work). Brings up capture pipeline, TC358743 bridge,
309	     * backlight, and parks the panel in UI-only mode. */
310	    ISC_Capture_Initialize();
311	    ISC_Capture_SetFrameCallback(on_frame_done, 0);
312	    TC358743_Initialize();
313	    XLCDC_EnableBacklight();
314	    lcd_unbind();
315	
316	    for (;;)
317	    {
318	        TC358743_Tasks();
319	        reconcile();
320	        vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(VIDEO_POLL_MS));
321	    }
322	}
323	
324	/* ─── Public API ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────── */
325	
326	static StackType_t  s_task_stack[VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS];
327	static StaticTask_t s_task_tcb;
328	
329	void Video_Initialize(void)
330	{
331	    TaskHandle_t h = xTaskCreateStatic(video_task,
332	                                       "VideoTask",
333	                                       VIDEO_TASK_STACK_WORDS,
334	                                       NULL,
335	                                       VIDEO_TASK_PRIORITY,
336	                                       s_task_stack,
337	                                       &s_task_tcb);
338	    PerfLog_RegisterTaskForHighwater(PERF_TASK_VIDEO, h);
339	}
340	
341	void Video_CaptureEnable(void)  { s_capture_enabled = true;  }
342	void Video_CaptureDisable(void) { s_capture_enabled = false; }
343	
344	void Video_DisplayShow(void)    { s_display_shown = true;    }
345	void Video_DisplayHide(void)    { s_display_shown = false;   }
346	
347	void Video_SetWindow(uint32_t x, uint32_t y, uint32_t dst_w, uint32_t dst_h)
348	{
349	    window_t w = { x, y, dst_w, dst_h };
350	    s_window = w;
351	    /* Force a re-bind on next reconcile if we're currently shown. */
352	    s_display_bound = false;
353	}
354	
355	bool Video_SubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
356	{
357	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
358	
359	    bool ok = false;
360	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
361	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
362	    {
363	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q) { ok = true; break; }     /* already in */
364	        if (s_subscribers[i] == NULL)
365	        {
366	            s_subscribers[i] = q;
367	            ok = true;
368	            break;
369	        }
370	    }
371	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
372	
373	    if (!ok) { LOG_ERROR("VIDEO: subscriber table full (max %u)\r\n",
374	                         (unsigned)VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS); }
375	    return ok;
376	}
377	
378	bool Video_UnsubscribeFrames(QueueHandle_t q)
379	{
380	    if (q == NULL) { return false; }
381	
382	    bool ok = false;
383	    taskENTER_CRITICAL();
384	    for (uint8_t i = 0u; i < VIDEO_MAX_SUBSCRIBERS; i++)
385	    {
386	        if (s_subscribers[i] == q)
387	        {
388	            s_subscribers[i] = NULL;
389	            ok = true;
390	            break;
391	        }
392	    }
393	    taskEXIT_CRITICAL();
394	    return ok;
395	}

397	void Video_GetFrameInfo(Video_FrameInfo *info)
398	{
399	    if (info == NULL) { return; }
400	    info->buffer          = (void *)(uintptr_t)s_latest_buffer;
401	    info->frame_count     = ISC_Capture_FrameCount();
402	    info->width           = s_src_w;
403	    info->height          = s_src_h;
404	    info->bytes_per_pixel = VIDEO_BYTES_PER_PIXEL;
405	}
```

```text
15	/* Sized to 720p60 (current TC358743 ceiling). Pool lives in .region_nocache
16	 * (16 MB total); 4×1280×720×3 ≈ 11 MB fits with headroom. Bumping to 1080p
17	 * would require either growing ram_nocache in ddram.ld or going back to
18	 * cached + per-frame D-cache invalidate. */
19	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_W        1280u
20	#define ISC_CAP_MAX_H        720u
21	#define ISC_CAP_BPP          3u    /* BYPASS+PACKED32+RMS=1+BPS=FORTY: dense BGR888 3 B/pixel */
22	/* At 60 fps depth N gives a subscriber holding a buffer pointer N×16.6 ms
23	 * before the producer laps. 4 → ~50 ms read window. */
24	#define ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS  4u
25	/* HSFREQRANGE for SAM9X75 D-PHY RX. SAM9X75 is DWC Gen3 per Linux DT
26	 * (snps,dw-dphy-rx with snps,phy_type=<0>, 8-bit bus). For 972 Mbps/lane
27	 * in Gen3 table: 0x0A (band covers ≤1000 Mbps). Was 0x14 at 297 Mbps
28	 * (works in both Gen2 and Gen3 — bands coincide there). Changes with bitrate. */
29	#define ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE  0x0Au
30	
31	/* Uncached so CPU readers (detectors, recorder) see ISC DMA writes without
32	 * cache maintenance. Trade: every read is a DDR fetch — fine for sparse
33	 * patch sampling, would matter for a full-frame scan. */
34	static __attribute__((__section__(".region_nocache")))
35	       __attribute__((__aligned__(32)))
36	       uint8_t g_framebuffer[ISC_CAP_MAX_W * ISC_CAP_MAX_H * ISC_CAP_BPP * ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS];

48	static void isc_frame_done(uintptr_t ctx)
49	{
50	    /* The MCC ISC driver increments DrvISCObj.frameIndex before invoking
51	     * this callback (drv_isc.c ISC_Handler), so frameIndex now points at
52	     * the descriptor hardware is about to write. The just-completed
53	     * buffer is the previous slot in the descriptor ring. */
54	    DRV_ISC_OBJ *obj = (DRV_ISC_OBJ *)ctx;
55	    uint32_t n = obj->dmaDescSize;
56	    uint32_t completed = (obj->frameIndex == 0u)
57	                       ? (n - 1u)
58	                       : (obj->frameIndex - 1u);
59	    uint32_t addr = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_framebuffer
60	                  + completed * obj->dma.size;
61	
62	    g_frame_count++;
63	    ISC_Capture_FrameCallback cb = s_frame_cb;
64	    if (cb != NULL) { cb(g_frame_count, addr, s_frame_ctx); }
65	}

70	    s_frame_cb  = cb;

73	void ISC_Capture_Initialize(void)
74	{
75	    iscObj    = DRV_ISC_Initialize();
76	    csi2dcObj = DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize();
77	    csiObj    = DRV_CSI_Initalize();
78	
79	    if (iscObj == NULL || csi2dcObj == NULL || csiObj == NULL)
80	    {
81	        LOG_ERROR("ISC_Capture: driver init returned NULL\r\n");
82	        return;
83	    }
84	
85	    /* BYPASS RLP + IMODE=PACKED32 + BPS=FORTY + CSI2DC RMS=1:
86	     * CSI2DC byte-stream packs the MIPI RGB888 stream per CSI-2
87	     * Recommended Memory Storage spec (Table 49.27): four BGR pixels
88	     * across 12 bytes, dense 3 B/pixel BGR888 in memory. ISC PACKED32
89	     * DMA writes 4 bytes per CSI2DC word (samples-per-row =
90	     * (width × 3) / 4, COLMAX programmed accordingly). LCDC reads
91	     * natively in RGB_888_PACKED mode (memory order B, G, R per pixel
92	     * — Table 44.26). 25% less DDR bandwidth than the ARGB_8888 /
93	     * BGRX32 path (capture write + display read both shrink) while
94	     * preserving full RGB888 quality for vision consumers. */
95	    iscObj->inputFormat           = ISC_INPUT_FORMAT_TYPE;  /* RGB */
96	    iscObj->inputBits             = DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_40_BIT; /* BPS=FORTY */
97	    iscObj->rlpMode               = ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_BYPASS;
98	    iscObj->layout                = ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED8;
99	    iscObj->bayerPattern          = ISC_BAYER_PATTERN_TYPE;
100	    iscObj->enableMIPI            = ISC_ENABLE_MIPI_INTERFACE;
101	    iscObj->enableVideoMode       = ISC_ENABLE_VIDEO_MODE;
102	    iscObj->enableProgressiveMode = ISC_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_MODE;
103	    iscObj->enableScaling         = ISC_ENABLE_SCALING;
104	    iscObj->dpc.enableDPC         = ISC_ENABLE_DPC;
105	    iscObj->dpc.enableGDC         = ISC_ENABLE_GDC;
106	    iscObj->dpc.enableBLC         = ISC_ENABLE_BLC;
107	    iscObj->cbc.enableCBC         = ISC_ENABLE_BRIGHTNESS_CONTRAST;
108	    iscObj->whiteBalance.enableWB = ISC_ENABLE_WHITE_BALANCE;
109	    iscObj->gamma.enableGamma     = ISC_ENABLE_GAMMA;
110	    iscObj->enableHistogram       = ISC_ENABLE_HISTOGRAM;
111	    iscObj->dmaDescSize           = (uint8_t)ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS;
112	    iscObj->dma.callback          = isc_frame_done;
113	
114	    /* DRV_CSI_Initalize hardcodes csiBitRate = 0x16; override here. */
115	    csiObj->csiBitRate = ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE;
116	
117	    /* TC358743 uses continuous-clock mode (TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE).
118	     * CSI2DC must match: MIPIFRN = 0 (free-running). MCC default is gated
119	     * (false -> MIPIFRN=1); mismatch leaves CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP stuck. */
120	    csi2dcObj->enableMIPIFreeRun = true;
121	
122	    /* PA=0 (VPCFGR bit 14): leave video pipe output LSB-aligned. PA=1 is
123	     * intended for 10/12-bit Bayer sensors being packed onto ISC's 12-bit
124	     * internal data bus. */
125	    csi2dcObj->videoPipeAlign = false;
126	
127	    LOG_INFO("ISC_Capture: initialized\r\n");
128	}

167	bool ISC_Capture_Configure(uint32_t width, uint32_t height)
168	{
169	    if (g_running) { ISC_Capture_Stop(); }
170	
171	    if (width == 0u || height == 0u
172	        || width > ISC_CAP_MAX_W || height > ISC_CAP_MAX_H)
173	    {
174	        LOG_ERROR("ISC_Capture: %lux%lu out of range\r\n",
175	                  (unsigned long)width, (unsigned long)height);
176	        return false;
177	    }
178	
179	    uint32_t frame_size = width * height * ISC_CAP_BPP;
180	
181	    csiObj->csiFrameWidth  = width;
182	    csiObj->csiFrameHeight = height;
183	    csiObj->csiFps         = 60u;
184	
185	    /* imageWidth/Height stay in pixel units. With RMS=0 + PACKED32, the
186	     * ISC per-row sample counter is also in pixel units (1 sample = 1
187	     * 32-bit word = 1 pixel), so COLMAX = width - 1 programmed below. */
188	    iscObj->imageWidth   = (uint16_t)width;
189	    iscObj->imageHeight  = (uint16_t)height;
190	    iscObj->outputWidth  = (uint16_t)width;
191	    iscObj->outputHeight = (uint16_t)height;
192	    iscObj->dma.address0 = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_framebuffer;
193	    iscObj->dma.size     = frame_size;
194	
195	    g_frame_count = 0u;
196	
197	    /* Configure order mirrors emirror's working CAMERA_Open:
198	     * CSI2DC -> CSI -> ISC. RX side must be ready before source
199	     * transmits, so the D-PHY catches the LP11->HS transition. */
200	    if (!DRV_CSI2DC_Configure(csi2dcObj))
201	    {
202	        LOG_ERROR("ISC_Capture: DRV_CSI2DC_Configure failed\r\n");
203	        return false;
204	    }
205	    if (!DRV_CSI_Configure(csiObj))
206	    {
207	        LOG_ERROR("ISC_Capture: DRV_CSI_Configure failed\r\n");
208	        return false;
209	    }
210	    if (DRV_ISC_Configure(iscObj) != 0u)
211	    {
212	        LOG_ERROR("ISC_Capture: DRV_ISC_Configure failed\r\n");
213	        return false;
214	    }
215	
216	    /* Program PFE crop window to the configured image size. The MCC
217	     * ISC driver defines ISC_PFE_Crop_Area() but never calls it — the
218	     * PFE_CFG1/2 registers stay at reset value 0, which tells the PFE
219	     * to expect a 1×1 pixel frame. Setting the crop values alone isn't
220	     * enough: the Linux mchp-isc driver also sets COLEN+ROWEN in
221	     * PFE_CFG0 to activate the crop window; without these bits the
222	     * PFE doesn't properly detect line/frame boundaries and VD never
223	     * fires. DRV_ISC_Configure does NOT touch these registers, so our
224	     * writes here persist through to capture start.
225	     *
226	     * Note: emirror/libcamera does NOT call DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA
227	     * separately; DRV_ISC_Configure calls it internally (line 381 of
228	     * drv_isc.c). A second explicit call would reset DCFG back to the
229	     * MCC BEATS8 default and clobber our overrides. Don't add one. */
230	    /* RMS=1 byte-stream + IMODE=PACKED32: each ISC sample is one 32-bit
231	     * CSI2DC word; the byte stream emits (width × 3) bytes per row =
232	     * (width × 3 / 4) sample-words. COLMAX is samples-1 in this mode. */
233	    uint32_t isc_samples_per_row = (width * ISC_CAP_BPP) / 4u;
234	    ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG1 = ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMIN(0u)
235	                           | ISC_PFE_CFG1_COLMAX(isc_samples_per_row - 1u);
236	    ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG2 = ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMIN(0u)
237	                           | ISC_PFE_CFG2_ROWMAX((uint32_t)height - 1u);
238	    ISC_REGS->ISC_PFE_CFG0 |= ISC_PFE_CFG0_COLEN_1 | ISC_PFE_CFG0_ROWEN_1;
239	
240	    /* Override ISC DMA config:
241	     *  - IMODE=PACKED32: each ISC sample = one 32-bit CSI2DC VP word; DMA
242	     *    writes 4 bytes per sample to DDR. With RMS=1's byte-packed stream
243	     *    that works out to (width × 3)/4 samples per row × 4 B/sample =
244	     *    width × 3 bytes per row = dense 3 B/pixel BGR. PACKED8 would only
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 16:08:31Z)**_

I now have the full architecture. Here's what's actually happening:

**Overlay in snapshot:** `draw_overlay()` in [cv_marvin_v1.c:406](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L406) burns the rings **into the shared capture ring buffer**. The strips are emitted *before* that call (lines 397–404, deliberately "pre-overlay"), so today **strips are clean and the snapshot picks up rings** — the reverse of what you want. The snapshot (`emit_snapshot`) copies `s_latest_buffer`, which is the same buffer the CV task drew rings into and the same one HEO displays.

**Tearing (yes, it's possible):** The capture is a **4-deep nocache ring** ([isc_capture.c:24](firmware/marvin/default/src/video/isc_capture.c#L24)) — ISC laps a buffer in ~50 ms at 60 fps. The snapshot does a single **2.7 MB memcpy from uncached DDR** (every byte a raw DDR fetch, no burst caching), with the ISC DMA, HEO readout, and CV task all contending for the bus. If that copy ever exceeds the ~50 ms lap window, ISC overwrites the tail of the buffer mid-copy → tearing. The journal's "coherent copy" reasoning compared the lap to the *emit* time, but the relevant race is the lap vs the *copy* — and the copy is the slow part. So intermittent tearing is expected, not impossible.

This spans firmware (cv_marvin_v1, perf_log, RX command, records) + host + GUI, with real design forks, so let me plan it and confirm a couple of decisions.

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How should a clean (overlay-free) snapshot be produced?**

Options:
- **Auto around snapshot (Recommended)** - Firmware gains an overlay on/off command. The marvin-perf Snapshot button automatically turns the overlay OFF, waits a few frames so the ring buffers are clean, captures, then turns it back ON. One click → clean snapshot; panel/strips keep rings the rest of the time. Also expose a manual toggle in the GUI.
- **Manual toggle only** - Firmware gains an overlay on/off command; GUI gets an Overlay on/off button. You turn it off yourself before snapshotting, then back on. Simpler firmware/host (no auto-sequencing), but snapshotting is a 3-step dance.
- **Firmware self-contained** - emit_snapshot disables the overlay, waits for clean frames, and re-enables it entirely inside firmware (no host involvement). Adds a perf_log→detector code dependency / layering coupling.

**Should the physical LVDS panel keep showing the target rings?**

Options:
- **Keep rings on panel (Recommended)** - Overlay stays drawn into the capture buffer (panel keeps the live calibration rings). Strips get rings by reordering the strip-emit to after draw_overlay. Snapshot cleaned via the toggle. Least restructuring.
- **Panel can be clean** - Move the overlay out of the capture buffer entirely: draw rings only onto the strip copies for the viewer. Snapshot + panel are then always clean with no toggle needed for the snapshot. Cleaner architecture, but the physical panel loses its live alignment rings.


**Answer:** Auto around snapshot (Recommended), panel can be clean. For now, let's keep the LVDS display clean of our overlay. Although I might want ability to add for demo purposes in the future

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-14 16:12:50Z)**_

Here's the concrete picture.

## How deep can you go, and at what cost

One 720p buffer = **2.76 MB**. The pool lives in `.region_nocache`, which is **16 MiB** (`ddram.ld:15`, `LENGTH = 0x01000000`). The ISC driver's descriptor array is capped at **`ISC_MAX_DMA_DESC = 10`** (`drv_isc.h:9`), and `dmaDescSize` is just `ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS`.

| Buffers | nocache used | Lap window @60fps | Change required |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 (today) | 11.1 MB | ~50 ms | — |
| **5** | 13.8 MB | ~66 ms | **one line**: `ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS 5` |
| 6 | 16.6 MB | ~83 ms | one line, but only ~190 KB headroom left — risky |
| 7–10 | 19–28 MB | ~100–166 ms | **grow `ram_nocache` in `ddram.ld`** |
| >10 | — | — | also bump `ISC_MAX_DMA_DESC` |

So:

- **4 → 5: trivial.** One-line change, comfortable headroom, driver already supports it. Buys ~16 ms.
- **6: borderline.** It arithmetically fits, but `.region_nocache` is *also* used by the XLCDC and UDPHS drivers (grep hits in `drv_gfx_xlcdc.c`, `drv_usb_udphs_device.c`), so leaving ~190 KB is asking for a hard-to-debug overlap. I wouldn't without auditing those.
- **7–10: moderate.** Edit the linker — `ram_nocache` is at `0x20000000`, length `0x01000000`; you have 240 MB of DDR so the window can grow, but you have to make sure it doesn't collide with the cached region's layout. Driver supports up to 10 descriptors before *that* constant also needs bumping.

## The catch

A deeper ring only **widens the tear window — it doesn't close it.** The variable is the 2.76 MB *uncached* copy: every byte is a raw DDR fetch with no burst caching, contending with the ISC writer and HEO readout. If that copy ever spikes past the lap window (even 83 ms), you still tear. Going 4→5 lowers the probability; it's not a guarantee.

The guaranteed fixes are orthogonal to depth:
1. **Lap-detect + retry** — record `frame_count` before/after the copy; if ISC advanced past the safe slot count, redo the copy (bounded retries). Cheap, robust, no memory cost. *This is what I'd lead with.*
2. **Copy faster** — DMA/`memcpy` from a cached alias with one invalidate, instead of byte-at-a-time uncached reads. Bigger change.

My recommendation: bump to **5 buffers** (free insurance) **and** add lap-detect-retry in `emit_snapshot`. The deeper buffer makes a retry almost never needed; the retry makes tearing actually impossible.

Want me to fold "bump to 5 + lap-detect retry" into the plan as the tearing fix? And note that since you chose "panel can be clean," the CV task stops drawing into the capture buffer at all — which removes one of the bus contenders during the copy as a bonus.

```text
125	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
126	{
127	    perf_hdr_t hdr;

129	    uint8_t    chord_open;            /* 0/1 — window currently accepting */
130	    uint8_t    chord_mask;            /* mask accumulated in the open window */
131	    uint16_t   chord_age_ms;          /* now_ms - chord_start_ms when open */
132	    uint8_t    note_q_count;
133	    uint8_t    note_head_mask;        /* mask of front-of-queue (next to fire) */
134	    uint8_t    note_tail_mask;        /* union of all queued note masks */
135	    uint8_t    reserved;
136	    uint32_t   note_head_at_ms;       /* assert_at_ms of front-of-queue */
137	    uint8_t    strum_q_count;
138	    uint8_t    strum_head_mask;
139	    uint8_t    strum_dir_next;        /* 0=none, 1=down, 2=up — next strum */
140	    uint8_t    reserved2;
141	    uint32_t   strum_head_at_ms;      /* strum_at_ms of front-of-queue */
142	    uint8_t    frets_active;          /* asserted mask, pre-strum overlay */
143	    uint8_t    strum_active;          /* 0/1 — strum pulse currently held */
144	    uint8_t    release_pending_mask;  /* frets with pending release timer */
145	    uint8_t    publish_mask;          /* final wire output mask */
146	    uint32_t   strum_release_at_ms;   /* deadline for current strum pulse */
147	    uint32_t   release_min_at_ms;     /* earliest pending-release deadline */
148	} perf_rec_timing_t;
149	
150	/* PERF_REC_DROP — drain task emits at 1 Hz. Counters are cumulative
151	 * since session start; host computes deltas. */
152	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
153	{
154	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
155	    uint32_t   dropped_state;
156	    uint32_t   dropped_strip;
157	    uint32_t   dropped_sink;

161	/* PERF_REC_TASK_HIGHWATER — periodic stack high-water dump. task_id is
162	 * a stable enum mirrored in the host decoder; words is the
163	 * uxTaskGetStackHighWaterMark return (StackType_t units).
164	 *
165	 * Marvin-owned tasks (0..5) are registered at task creation. IDLE is
166	 * the FreeRTOS idle task (xTaskGetIdleTaskHandle) — its run_time_counter
167	 * is what makes absolute CPU% computable on the host
168	 * (1 - idle_delta / Σ_all_delta). MCC tasks (LEGATO..APP) are looked up
169	 * by string name with xTaskGetHandle from the perf-drain task at startup.
170	 * OTHER is a pseudo-slot: not a real task, just an aggregate of "all
171	 * tasks not in this enum" that the drain emits each runtime cycle so
172	 * per-window CPU% adds to 100. HWM is meaningless for OTHER (no single
173	 * stack); the runtime-side producer emits TASK_RUNTIME for OTHER but
174	 * skips TASK_HIGHWATER. */
175	typedef enum
176	{
177	    PERF_TASK_VIDEO          = 0,
178	    PERF_TASK_CV_MARVIN_V1   = 1,
179	    PERF_TASK_DETECTOR_DRAIN = 2,
180	    PERF_TASK_TIMING         = 3,
181	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_LINK = 4,
182	    PERF_TASK_PERF_DRAIN     = 5,
183	    PERF_TASK_IDLE           = 6,
184	    PERF_TASK_LEGATO         = 7,
185	    PERF_TASK_XLCDC          = 8,
186	    PERF_TASK_MAXTOUCH       = 9,
187	    PERF_TASK_SYS_INPUT      = 10,
188	    PERF_TASK_USB_DEVICE     = 11,
189	    PERF_TASK_USB_HOST       = 12,
190	    PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_UDPHS  = 13,
191	    PERF_TASK_DRV_USB_HOST   = 14,
192	    PERF_TASK_APP            = 15,
193	    PERF_TASK_OTHER          = 16,
194	    PERF_TASK_FRETBOARD_RX   = 17,
195	} perf_task_id_t;
196	
197	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
198	{
199	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
200	    uint8_t    task_id;
201	    uint8_t    reserved[3];
202	    uint32_t   words;
203	} perf_rec_task_highwater_t;
204	
205	/* PERF_REC_STRIP — variable-size BGR888 region of interest, kind-tagged.
206	 * Today's producers emit SENSING (row through the sensor patches) and
207	 * STRIKE (row through the strum trigger zone), each 240×32 once per ISC
208	 * frame; SNAPSHOT carries a full frame as a top-to-bottom sequence of
209	 * full-width bands sharing one frame_epoch (last band flags LAST).
210	 * Future kinds (SCORE, MINIMAP, etc.) plug into the same record type —
211	 * adding one is an enum entry plus a producer; no schema bump.
212	 *
213	 * Wire payload size is HDR + 12 B body + w*h*PERF_STRIP_BPP bytes,
214	 * tightly packed. The queue slot is sized to PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES; the
215	 * drain task computes the on-wire length from (w, h) and frames only
216	 * what's used. */
217	typedef enum
218	{
219	    PERF_STRIP_SENSING  = 0,
220	    PERF_STRIP_STRIKE   = 1,
221	    PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT = 2,
222	} perf_strip_kind_t;
223	
224	/* Strip flags byte (perf_rec_strip_t.flags). SNAPSHOT producers set LAST on
225	 * the final (bottom) band so the host knows the frame is complete without a
226	 * separate end marker. Zero for SENSING/STRIKE. */
227	#define PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST  0x01u
228	
229	#define PERF_STRIP_BPP        3u
230	
231	/* Wire-bound on the strip pixel-data size. Two stacked caps determine
232	 * the maximum payload a strip can carry:
233	 *
234	 *   1. Wire LEN field is u16 → max payload 65535 bytes
235	 *      → max pixel = 65535 − HDR(16) − BODY(12) = 65507
236	 *   2. UDPHS DMA single-transfer cap is
237	 *      DRV_USB_UDPHS_DMA_MAX_TRANSFER_SIZE × 64 KB
238	 *      (currently 2 × 64 KB = 128 KB; well above the LEN cap)
239	 *
240	 * The u16 LEN field is the binding constraint. Set at 65000 to land just
241	 * under it with a small margin. Producers may use any (w, h) shape as
242	 * long as w * h * PERF_STRIP_BPP <= PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES.
243	 *
244	 * Practical strip-size envelope (pixel area = w*h ≤ ~21666):
245	 *   720×30  640×33  480×45  320×64  290×72
246	 *
247	 * Buffer footprint scales with this:
248	 *   pool      = PL_STRIP_POOL_SIZE × (28 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
249	 *   sink ring = SINK_TX_RING_DEPTH × round_up_64(36 + PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES)
250	 * Together ~585 KB BSS at 65000; trivially fits in the 240 MB cached DDR.
251	 *
252	 * To go beyond u16 LEN, the wire format itself needs a schema break (LEN
253	 * → u32). Don't do that lightly — at 60 fps × 65 KB = ~3.9 MB/s, this cap
254	 * already lines up with what the wire can sustainably carry. */
255	#define PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES  65000u
256	
257	#define PERF_STRIP_HDR_BYTES  (sizeof(perf_hdr_t) + 12u)   /* hdr + body */
258	
259	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
260	{
261	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
262	    uint16_t   x, y;          /* top-left in source frame */
263	    uint16_t   w, h;          /* per-record dimensions */
264	    uint8_t    kind;          /* perf_strip_kind_t */
265	    uint8_t    flags;         /* PERF_STRIP_FLAG_* */
266	    uint8_t    reserved[2];
267	    uint8_t    bgr[PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES];   /* sized to max in queue slot */
268	} perf_rec_strip_t;
269	
270	/* PERF_REC_TASK_RUNTIME — per-task snapshot of state, priority, and
271	 * cumulative run-time counter. Drain task emits one record per known
272	 * task at 1 Hz alongside DROP and TASK_HIGHWATER. Host computes per-
273	 * window CPU% as Δrun_time_counter[task] / ΣΔrun_time_counter. */
274	typedef enum
275	{
276	    PERF_TASK_STATE_RUNNING   = 0,
277	    PERF_TASK_STATE_READY     = 1,
278	    PERF_TASK_STATE_BLOCKED   = 2,
279	    PERF_TASK_STATE_SUSPENDED = 3,
280	    PERF_TASK_STATE_DELETED   = 4,
281	    PERF_TASK_STATE_INVALID   = 5,
282	} perf_task_state_t;
283	
284	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
285	{
286	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
287	    uint8_t    task_id;            /* perf_task_id_t */
288	    uint8_t    state;              /* perf_task_state_t (mirrors eTaskState) */
289	    uint8_t    priority;           /* uxCurrentPriority */
290	    uint8_t    reserved;
291	    uint32_t   run_time_counter;   /* low 32 bits of ulRunTimeCounter */
292	    uint32_t   reserved2;
293	} perf_rec_task_runtime_t;

295	/* PERF_REC_DETECTOR_CONFIG — cv_marvin_v1 per-fret configuration. Static

300	 * representation on both sides. Used by the host to render sample
301	 * dots / threshold reference lines onto STRIP canvases. */

303	{
304	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
305	    uint16_t   sensor_hx[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor x per fret */
306	    uint16_t   sensor_hy[FRET_COUNT];          /* hold-sensor y per fret */
307	    uint16_t   sensor_ex[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor x per fret */
308	    uint16_t   sensor_ey[FRET_COUNT];          /* edge-sensor y per fret */
309	    float      hold_thresh;                    /* CV_HOLD_THRESH (brightness) */
310	    float      hold_release_frac;              /* CV_HOLD_RELEASE_FRAC */
311	    float      edge_thresh;                    /* CV_EDGE_THRESH */
312	    float      color_target_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret target weights */
313	    float      color_target_g[FRET_COUNT];
314	    float      color_target_r[FRET_COUNT];
315	    float      color_reject_b[FRET_COUNT];     /* per-fret reject weights */
316	    float      color_reject_g[FRET_COUNT];
317	    float      color_reject_r[FRET_COUNT];
318	} perf_rec_detector_config_t;

320	/* PERF_REC_ACTUATOR — emitted on every FretboardLink_Send call (i.e. on
321	 * intent), one record per call. Closes the gap between TIMING.publish_mask
322	 * (intent on the timing pipeline side) and FBL_SEND STAMP (a byte hit the
323	 * USB DMA): with multiple producers (timing_pipeline, manual_control, future
324	 * game_state_controller per spec §4.8), the wire byte alone doesn't say
325	 * who asserted what.

327	 * intended_mask: what the producer asked for this Send (low 7 bits).
328	 * asserted_mask: what's currently held on the link (last byte queued).
329	 * strum_dir: from the bit pattern (0=none, 1=down, 2=up).
330	 * producer_id: perf_actuator_producer_t — the arbitration signal that's
331	 *              invisible on the wire today.
332	 * last_ack_*:  most recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE result and timestamp,
333	 *              snapshotted at Send-time so the host can compute transport-
334	 *              side latency without joining FBL_SEND/CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE
335	 *              stamps (still useful, but redundant for the common case). */
336	typedef enum
337	{
338	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_NONE   = 0,
339	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_TIMING = 1,
340	    PERF_ACTUATOR_PRODUCER_MANUAL = 2,
341	} perf_actuator_producer_t;
342	
343	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
344	{
345	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
346	    uint8_t    intended_mask;
347	    uint8_t    asserted_mask;
348	    uint8_t    strum_dir;            /* 0=none, 1=down, 2=up */
349	    uint8_t    producer_id;          /* perf_actuator_producer_t */
350	    int32_t    last_ack_result;      /* USB_HOST_CDC_RESULT_*, signed for safety */
351	    uint64_t   last_ack_ts_counter;  /* SYS_TIME at most-recent CDC_WRITE_COMPLETE */
352	} perf_rec_actuator_t;
353	
354	/* PERF_REC_FRETBOARD_RAW — one record per parsed 17-byte fretboard data
355	 * frame (firmware/fretboard/data_stream.c). The 5×u16 ADC values are 12-bit
356	 * unsigned (0–4095, lower = brighter sensor) indexed by fret_t (G/R/Y/B/O).
357	 * Fretboard emits at ~240 Hz; with video at 60 Hz the same frame_epoch
358	 * value tags ~4 consecutive records — ts_counter (stamped by hdr_fill at
359	 * record-emit time) disambiguates within the frame.
360	 *
361	 * fb_sample_seq and applied_mask are stamped by the fretboard itself and
362	 * carried on the wire: the sequence counter (one per fretboard tick) lets the
363	 * host reconstruct true sample order and detect frames dropped in transit,
364	 * and applied_mask is the actuator bitmask the fretboard was driving during
365	 * this very scan — so sensor and actuator state are paired atomically at the
366	 * source instead of joined across marvin's TX/RX clocks. Default-disabled at
367	 * boot like the other high-rate types. */
368	typedef struct __attribute__((packed))
369	{
370	    perf_hdr_t hdr;
371	    uint16_t   adc[FRET_COUNT];      /* 5 × 2 = 10 B */
372	    uint32_t   fb_sample_seq;        /* fretboard tick counter (monotonic) */
373	    uint8_t    applied_mask;         /* actuator bitmask driven this scan */
374	    uint8_t    reserved;
375	} perf_rec_fretboard_raw_t;

377	/* ─── Host→device commands ───────────────────────────────────────────────────

379	 * Wrapped in the same SOF/LEN/CRC framer as TX records. Magic is distinct

383	
384	#define PERF_CMD_HDR_MAGIC   0x4D43u   /* 'M','C' little-endian */

398
```

```bash
EOF
```

```md
# Move target-ring overlay off the capture buffer (clean snapshot + clean panel, ringed strips)

## Context

The CV detector draws per-fret "target rings" at each sample point. Today
`draw_overlay()` ([cv_marvin_v1.c:406](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c#L406))
burns those rings **into the shared ISC capture buffer** — the same buffer the
LVDS panel displays (via HEO) and the same one the perf-log snapshot copies. The
SENSING/STRIKE strips are emitted *before* that call, so today's behavior is the
inverse of what's wanted: **strips are clean, the panel and snapshot carry rings.**

Desired end state:
- **Full-frame snapshot: clean** (no rings) — it's for offline OCR/analysis of GH3 screens.
- **Live LVDS panel: clean** (no rings) for now — keep the option to re-add a panel
  overlay for demos later.
- **Web-viewer strips: show the rings** — to verify sample-point alignment live.
- **A host/GUI toggle** to turn the strip rings on/off.

The fix follows directly: **never draw rings into the capture buffer.** Draw them
only onto the strip *copy* that ships to the viewer. That makes the snapshot and
panel inherently clean (no per-snapshot toggling needed), and the strips carry the
rings. (Capture stays at 4 buffers — 5 overflows the 16 MiB `.region_nocache` by
~1.1 MB once the 3.9 MB XLCDC framebuffer is accounted for. Tearing mitigation
deferred; captured screens are mostly static.)

## Approach

### Firmware

**`perf_log_records.h`** — new host→device command (commands don't affect the record
schema, so **no schema bump**):
- `PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY = 0x03u` in `perf_cmd_t`.
- `perf_cmd_set_overlay_t { perf_cmd_hdr_t hdr; uint32_t flags; }`.
- Flag bits: `PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP = 0x01` (viewer strip rings), `PERF_OVERLAY_PANEL = 0x02`
  (reserved — future LVDS demo overlay, no-op for now).

**`perf_log.c` / `perf_log.h`** — overlay-flag state + a prepacked strip emit:
- `static volatile uint32_t s_overlay_flags = PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP;` (strip rings on at boot)
  + `PerfLog_SetOverlayFlags(uint32_t)` / `PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags(void)`.
- `PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(uint32_t frame_epoch, perf_strip_kind_t kind, uint16_t x,
  uint16_t y, uint16_t w, uint16_t h, const uint8_t *pixels)` — claims a pool slot, fills
  the header, single `memcpy` of the already-tight `w*h*3` payload into the slot, queues.
  Same `type_enabled(PERF_REC_STRIP)` gating + drop-on-pool-empty as
  `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame`; factor the shared "claim slot / set header / enqueue"
  out of the existing strided version.

**`perf_log_rx.c`** — dispatch `PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY` → `PerfLog_SetOverlayFlags(cmd.flags)`
(already `#include`s `perf_log.h`; payload 8 B fits `PL_RX_PAYLOAD_MAX = 64`).

**`cv_marvin_v1.c`** — stop dirtying the capture buffer; composite rings onto the SENSING
strip copy instead:
- Promote the SENSING/STRIKE strip rects (the `265,300,185,32` / `212,395,290,32` magic
  numbers) to named constants; add `static uint8_t s_sensing_scratch[CV_SENSING_W *
  CV_SENSING_H * CV_BYTES_PER_PIXEL]`.
- Rework `draw_overlay` to take a target buffer + dims + origin:
  `draw_overlay(uint8_t *buf, uint16_t bw, uint16_t bh, uint16_t ox, uint16_t oy)`, drawing
  each ring/dot at `(s.hx - ox, s.hy - oy)` etc. `put_pixel_bgr`/`draw_ring`/`draw_filled_disk`
  already use `bw` as a tight stride — correct for the packed scratch; out-of-strip pixels clip.
- Replace the per-frame tail (lines ~397–406):
  - **STRIKE**: keep `PerfLog_EmitStripFromFrame(...)` (no sensors there → no rings).
  - **SENSING**: strided-copy the region into `s_sensing_scratch`; if
    `PerfLog_GetOverlayFlags() & PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP`, `draw_overlay(scratch, CV_SENSING_W,
    CV_SENSING_H, CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y)`; then `PerfLog_EmitStripPacked(...,
    CV_SENSING_X, CV_SENSING_Y, CV_SENSING_W, CV_SENSING_H, scratch)`.
  - **Delete** the `draw_overlay((uint8_t *)frame.buffer, ...)` call.
- Update the now-stale comments (the "pre-overlay / same pixels the detector consumed"
  note and the calibration-overlay block) to describe drawing onto the strip copy.

### Host (`tools/marvin-perf`)

- **`records.py`**: `PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY = 0x03`; `PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP`/`PERF_OVERLAY_PANEL`;
  `encode_set_overlay_payload(flags)` mirroring `encode_set_mask_payload`.
- **`web/live.py`**: `set_overlay(enabled: bool)` — require active session, send
  `frame_encode(encode_set_overlay_payload(PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP if enabled else 0))`, track
  `overlay_enabled` in `_State`, `_post("overlay", …)`; surface in `status()` + the `hello` payload.
- **`web/api.py`**: `OverlayRequest{enabled: bool}`; `POST /api/live/overlay` →
  `_LIVE.set_overlay` (409 if inactive).
- **`cli.py`**: small `set-overlay --port --on/--off` subcommand for parity with `set-mask`.

### GUI (`web/static`)

- `index.html`: an "◎ Overlay" toggle button in `#live-controls` (default on/active).
- `app.js`: `toggleOverlay()` → `POST /api/live/overlay`; reflect state from `hello`/`status`
  and a WS `overlay` event; enable/disable alongside the snapshot button on live start/stop.
- `styles.css`: active/inactive button state (reuse existing toolbar button conventions).

## Verification

- `uv run pytest` in `tools/marvin-perf`: new tests in `test_live.py` assert `set_overlay(True/False)`
  sends `frame_encode(encode_set_overlay_payload(PERF_OVERLAY_STRIP|0))` (mirror the existing
  `test_set_mask_round_trips_to_serial_send`), plus an `encode_set_overlay_payload` unit check.
- Firmware builds in MPLAB/XC32 (Greg's side) — not buildable here.
- On hardware: in the viewer, **Snapshot** now yields a clean GH3 screen (no rings) and the
  LVDS panel is clean; the SENSING strip shows the rings; the **Overlay** toggle adds/removes
  rings from the strip live without touching the snapshot or panel.

## Out of scope / deferred
- Capture-buffer depth bump (stays 4 — 5 overflows nocache) and snapshot tearing retry.
- Re-adding a panel/LVDS overlay for demos (the `PERF_OVERLAY_PANEL` bit is reserved for it).
```

Done. Here's what landed.

## Summary

The target rings no longer touch the capture buffer — they're drawn only onto the **SENSING strip copy** that ships to the viewer. So the snapshot and the LVDS panel are now inherently clean (no per-snapshot toggling), and the strips carry the rings, with a host/GUI on/off toggle.

**Firmware** (not built/flashed — needs MPLAB/XC32 on your side):
- [cv_marvin_v1.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/detector/cv_marvin_v1.c) — dropped the `draw_overlay(frame.buffer)` call; SENSING row-copies into a scratch, paints rings there (when enabled), and ships via the new `PerfLog_EmitStripPacked`. STRIKE stays a clean copy. Strip rects are named constants; `draw_overlay` translates coords by the strip origin.
- [perf_log.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.c)/[.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log.h) — factored the strip slot logic into `strip_slot_claim`/`commit`; added `PerfLog_EmitStripPacked` + `s_overlay_flags` (boots STRIP-on) + get/set.
- [perf_log_records.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_records.h)/[perf_log_rx.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/perf_log/perf_log_rx.c) — `PERF_CMD_SET_OVERLAY` (0x03) with `STRIP`/`PANEL` flag bits. **No schema bump.** `PANEL` reserved for the future LVDS demo overlay.

**Host + GUI** (verified): `encode_set_overlay_payload`, `live.set_overlay`, `POST /api/live/overlay`, `marvin-perf set-overlay --on/--off`, and a "◎ Overlay" toggle in the live toolbar. **140 tests pass**; app/route/CLI smoke-checked.

**Decisions captured in the journal:**
- Capture stays at **4 buffers** — 5 overflows the 16 MiB nocache region by ~1.1 MB (XLCDC framebuffer takes ~3.9 MB there). Tearing-retry deferred since your captures are static.
- LVDS kept clean now; the `PERF_OVERLAY_PANEL` bit is the hook for a demo overlay later.

Two notes worth flagging:
1. **The hang earlier:** I never root-caused it (it became non-reproducible). Nothing in this change touches that path, so if it recurs, flag it and I'll dig into the USB-device CDC enumeration/`emit_snapshot` path.
2. Nothing is committed (per project rules) — say the word and I'll commit firmware + host + journal together.

```text
173	def cmd_snapshot(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
174	    """Trigger a full-frame snapshot and save it for offline analysis.
175	
176	    Sends PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT, reassembles the returned SNAPSHOT band strips
177	    into one frame, and writes <out>.bgr + <out>.json (+ <out>.png if Pillow
178	    is installed).
179	    """
180	    assembler = SnapshotAssembler()
181	    with SerialSource(args.port) as ser:
182	        ser.send_command(frame_encode(encode_snapshot_payload()))
183	        print("[snapshot] requested; waiting for bands…", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)
184	        snap = None
185	        for fb in iter_frames(_idle_chunks(ser, args.timeout)):
186	            rec = decode_record(fb.payload)
187	            if not isinstance(rec, Strip):
188	                continue
189	            snap = assembler.add(rec)
190	            if snap is not None:
191	                break
192	
193	    if snap is None:
194	        print(
195	            f"snapshot: no complete frame within {args.timeout:.1f}s idle timeout. "
196	            "Is marvin connected, HDMI locked, and the firmware schema current?",
197	            file=sys.stderr,
198	        )
199	        return 1
200	
201	    written = save_snapshot(snap, args.out)
202	    print(
203	        f"snapshot: {snap.width}×{snap.height} (frame_epoch {snap.frame_epoch}) → "
204	        + ", ".join(str(p) for p in written),
205	        file=sys.stderr,
206	    )
207	    return 0
```

Done.

## Summary

**PNG-only save.** Yes — PNG is lossless for the RGB pixels, so the `.bgr` was redundant. `save_snapshot` now writes **just `<stem>.png`**, with `frame_epoch` tucked into a PNG `tEXt` chunk instead of a `.json` sidecar. This applies to both the CLI and the GUI snapshot paths. Pillow moved from the `viewer` group to a **base dependency** since snapshot is a core feature.

**Auto-incrementing CLI filenames** — the "jump through screens" workflow:
```bash
marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/tty...        # → snapshots/snapshot-0001.png
marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/tty...        # → snapshots/snapshot-0002.png
marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/tty... --out shots/   # → shots/snapshot-0001.png
marvin-perf snapshot --port /dev/tty... --out hero.png # → exact file, verbatim
```
`--out` is now optional. Omitted or pointed at a directory → next free `snapshot-NNNN.png` (scans the dir, max+1, never clobbers). Ending in `.png` → used as-is.

**Tests:** PNG-only + lossless round-trip + tEXt-epoch checks, `_resolve_snapshot_out` cases (explicit/dir/default/gap-skip), and the live save now asserts `.png`. **145 passed**, no warnings.

Two things to flag:
- **GUI unchanged** beyond inheriting PNG-only: it still uses its auto-filled timestamped stem (one PNG per click). I scoped the auto-increment to the CLI as you asked. If repeated GUI clicks without editing the field would be a clobber annoyance for you, I can give the GUI the same `snapshot-NNNN.png` behavior — say the word.
- Nothing committed (per project rules). The firmware overlay work + this snapshot change + journal are all uncommitted whenever you want them landed.

```text
=== spec §4.8 gameplay engine ===
21:7. **Observe game state from the screen** — recognize current menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score-summary contexts via CV, expose high-level control verbs ("start single-player playthrough of song X", "advance menu", "exit to main menu") that translate into fret/strum command sequences sent through the same fretboard link.
45:| Fretboard link (FLEXCOM2 USART) | ✅ working; gameplay tested over the original USB CDC host link. Link rewired to a direct FLEXCOM2 UART for the Curiosity Hybrid board (no host-capable USB port); pending on-hardware re-validation. §4.3. |
46:| Timing pipeline (chord FIFO, strum) | ✅ working; end-to-end gameplay tested on Expert and Easy. §4.4. |
50:| Game-state awareness & high-level game control | 🚧 not started. §4.8, open Q10/Q11. |
99:   │      fretboard (PIC32CM6408)       │──────┘                │   │
135:| Game-state observation (menu / song-select / gameplay / pause / score) | marvin | CV on captured frames; emits typed game-state events on its own bus. §4.8. |
136:| Game catalog + menu metadata (song list, menu graph, recognized icons) | marvin | Compile-time tables and/or SD-card JSON. Drives the recognizer and the navigator. §4.8. |
137:| High-level game control (e.g., "start single-player song X") | marvin | Translates verbs into fret/strum sequences sent over the same fretboard link as gameplay commands. §4.8. |
175:| **fretboard board** (PIC32CM6408PL10048) | Sensor + actuator MCU | FLEXCOM1 USART (marvin PA28 TX / PA29 RX ↔ fretboard SERCOM1 PB01 RX / PB00 TX, 500 000 Bd 8N1, ring-buffer mode). |
302:**UI framework — open Q5.** Legato is already pulled in for capture init and could absorb the operator UI directly (heavy but in-tree). Alternative: a lightweight custom widget layer over GFX2D / direct framebuffer composition. Decision deferred until we attempt the first non-trivial screen (calibration overlay).
391:Independent of the SD recording path above (M4, not started), marvin can export a single full-resolution frame on demand over the existing perf-log USB CDC link. The host sends `PERF_CMD_SNAPSHOT`; the perf-drain task copies the current frame once into a staging buffer and streams it back as a top-to-bottom run of full-width `PERF_STRIP_SNAPSHOT` band records (each ≤ `PERF_STRIP_MAX_BYTES`), all sharing one `frame_epoch`, the last flagged `PERF_STRIP_FLAG_LAST`. Bands are written straight to the sink (bypassing the small strip pool) and paced by the wire; emit is not gated by the STRIP type mask. `marvin-perf snapshot` reassembles and saves the frame (`.bgr` + sidecar `.json`, plus `.png` via Pillow). This is the offline-study on-ramp for the game-state work (§4.8) — no in-runtime role.
403:### 4.8 Game-state awareness & control 🚧
405:Note on numbering: this subsystem is logically a peer of §4.2–§4.6 (a video-frame consumer that emits typed events plus a controller that issues actuator commands). It lives at §4.8 only to avoid renumbering existing sections referenced from the journal and milestones.
407:#### 4.8.1 Role
411:1. **Game-state observer.** Watch the screen; recognize what context the game is currently in — main menu, song-select, difficulty-select, in-game (gameplay), pause, score summary, etc. Surface that as typed events that the operator UI can render and the orchestrator below can act on.
412:2. **Game controller.** Expose high-level verbs ("start a single-player playthrough of song X on Hard", "go to the main menu", "select Practice mode"). Translate each verb into a sequence of fret/strum commands using the recognized current state and a known menu graph, monitor the screen for the expected state transitions, retry or back out on mismatch.
414:This is *not* the gameplay note-detection path (§4.2). cv_marvin_v1 plays notes during gameplay; the game-state module decides *what to play* at the session level (which song, which difficulty, which mode) and gets us there from any starting screen.
416:Recognition is being bootstrapped offline: the on-demand snapshot path (§4.6.8) collects a corpus of real GH3 screens, the detection algorithms (screen classification, then number/letter/score region readers) are prototyped host-side in Python against that corpus, and only the proven, simple GH3-specific logic is then ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module. Per Q10, the approach favors fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV — GH3's screens, fonts, and layouts are static.
418:#### 4.8.2 Module shape
424:- Issues control commands by writing fret/strum bitmasks into the same fretboard-link path used by gameplay. Whether this routes through the timing pipeline (§4.4) or bypasses it is open Q11.
426:#### 4.8.3 Game catalog & menu metadata
431:- **Menu graph.** Nodes = recognized game states; edges = button sequences that move between them (e.g., "main_menu → song_select" = `[STRUM_DOWN, STRUM_DOWN, GREEN]`). Used by the navigator to plan a verb.
432:- **Song catalog.** Per-supported-game list of songs with the menu coordinates needed to select each one (which difficulty submenu, ordinal position in the list, etc.). Possibly augmented with metadata (BPM, length, expected difficulty score) for UI display and for reference-data labeling.
436:Scope today: target is **one game** — Guitar Hero (Wii) — to validate the design. Adding a second game is a metadata addition (new template set + new menu graph + new song catalog), not a structural change.
438:#### 4.8.4 Interaction with other subsystems
440:- **Detection (§4.2):** independent. cv_marvin_v1 runs only when the game-state observer reports `gameplay`. Outside gameplay, cv_marvin_v1 may be disabled to free CPU.
441:- **Timing pipeline (§4.4):** during gameplay the timing pipeline drives the actuators from detector-state. Outside gameplay it's idle, and the game-state controller drives actuators directly. Coordination and arbitration between the two is open Q11.
442:- **Operator UI (§4.5):** consumes game-state events to display the current screen the game is on; offers verbs as buttons / song-list pickers.
443:- **Recording (§4.6):** game-state transitions are useful session metadata. Either annotated into `state.bin` as a side channel or a sibling file (`game_state.bin`). To be decided when the recorder lands.
444:- **Fretboard link (§4.3):** shared command path. The fretboard MCU does not know whether a press is "gameplay note" or "menu navigation" — they're the same wire bits.
446:#### 4.8.5 Open questions surfaced here
451:- **Q11** — Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline. Default is "they don't run at the same time" (gameplay vs menu), but the boundary needs to be explicit.
483:| `game_control_enable` | Game-state controller may issue actuator commands for menu navigation / session setup. Suppressed during `gameplay` state when timing pipeline is driving. |
503:9. **M9 — Game-state observer v0** (§4.8). Recognize main_menu / song_select / gameplay / pause / score states; surface as `xGameStateQueue` events. No control yet.
504:10. **M10 — Game-state control v0** (§4.8). High-level verbs ("start single-player song X") drive menu navigation through the same fretboard link.
522:| Q11 | Command-path arbitration between game-state controller and timing pipeline (§4.4 vs §4.8). Default working assumption: mutually exclusive (controller runs only outside `gameplay` state); may need richer arbitration if a game has gameplay-screen menus or pause overlays we want to drive. | Open. Decide at M10. |
```

```md
# GH3 (Wii) — Navigation Model

Working model of Guitar Hero III: Legends of Rock (Wii) screens and the menu
graph between them. This is the source artifact for the §4.8 game-state work:
the **observer** (M9) classifies the current screen and reads the highlighted
selection; the **controller** (M10) plans button sequences along the graph
edges below. See [`spec.md`](spec.md) §4.8.3 (game catalog & menu metadata).

Screen text is transcribed from operator narration; snapshots
(`tools/marvin-perf/snapshots/`, not committed) are the visual reference for
layout, highlight style, and classifier regions. Native capture is 720×480.

Status: **in progress** — populated screen-by-screen. `TBD` = not yet captured.

---

## Conventions

### Inputs
- **Strum up / strum down** — move the selection within a list.
- **GREEN** — confirm / enter the selected item.
- **RED** — back up one level.

(Bit names on the wire are the gameplay fret/strum masks; the controller emits
the same bits for menu navigation — the fretboard MCU doesn't distinguish menu
from gameplay. §4.8.4.)

### Highlight paradigms
How "selected" is presented drives what the observer reads. Two kinds so far:

- **static-list** — the list is painted at fixed screen positions; a highlight
  moves between rows. Observer reads *which row is lit*. (e.g. `main_menu`)
- **fixed-slot** — the selected item sits in a fixed, highlighted slot and the
  list scrolls underneath it. Observer reads *what occupies the highlight slot*.
  (e.g. `song_select`)

### Edge notation
An edge is `from → to : [inputs]`. `STRUM_DN×n` means n strum-downs. Moving to
list index `i` from the top (index 0) on a static list is `STRUM_DN×i, GREEN`.

---

## Screen catalog

### main_menu
- **snapshot:** snapshot-0001 (CAREER selected)
- **paradigm:** static-list (cursor moves; list fixed)
- **items (top → bottom, index):**
  0. CAREER
  1. CO-OP CAREER
  2. QUICKPLAY
  3. MULTIPLAYER
  4. TRAINING
  5. OPTIONS
  6. NINTENDO WFC
- **back (RED):** top level — no parent.
- **classifier hint:** TBD (a stable region/logo that uniquely IDs this screen).
- **leads to:**
  - CAREER → `career_*` (TBD)
  - CO-OP CAREER → TBD
  - QUICKPLAY → `quickplay_song_select` (TBD — confirm)
  - MULTIPLAYER → TBD
  - TRAINING → TBD
  - OPTIONS → TBD
  - NINTENDO WFC → TBD

### song_select  *(paradigm reference — details TBD)*
- **snapshot:** TBD
- **paradigm:** fixed-slot (selection fixed on screen; song list slides under it)
- **items:** TBD (song catalog → §4.8.3)
- **classifier hint / highlight slot region:** TBD

_(more screens added as captured)_

---

## Menu graph (edges)

| from | to | inputs | notes |
|------|----|--------|-------|
| main_menu | _(per item)_ | `STRUM_DN×index, GREEN` | static list, index per catalog above |
| _any_ | _(parent)_ | `RED` | back up one level |

_(filled in as destinations are confirmed)_

- Where each main-menu item leads, and the song-select model (fixed-slot read).
- Wrap-around behavior: does strum-down past the last item wrap to the first?
  (Affects shortest-path planning in the controller.)
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 17:56:24Z)**_

Good call to check. Quick answer on repo size:

- **You're fine.** `.git` at ~140 MB → ~180 MB after this. GitHub soft-warns around **1 GB** and only hard-blocks individual files **>100 MB** (our PNGs are ~0.5 MB). Plenty of headroom.
- The real caveat with binaries: they're **permanent in history and don't delta-compress** — so the thing to avoid is *re-committing changed versions of the same images* (each new version adds its full size forever) and unbounded corpus growth. These screens are write-once references, so that's not a concern. If the corpus ever balloons into the hundreds of MB (lots more modes/games), that's the trigger to migrate to LFS.

```bash
            name = (f"song_select__{idx:02d}_{slug(song)}" if 12<=snap<=50 else
                    f"song_select__bonus_{idx:02d}_{slug(song)}" if 51<=snap<=75 else None)
            if name:
                if not (screens/f"{name}.png").exists(): warn.append((snap,name))
                inner[3] = f"`gh3_screens/{name}.png`"
                line = "| " + " | ".join(inner) + " |"
    out.append(line)
doc.write_text("\n".join(out) + ("\n" if text.endswith("\n") else ""))
print("missing-file warnings:", warn or "none")
print("any 'snapshot-' refs left:", text.count("snapshot-"))
```

```text
316	---
317	
318	## Navigator notes (implementation)
319	
320	How the controller (M10) uses this map. Unmapped paths don't need modeling —
321	they're handled by recovery, not enumeration.
322	
323	- **Closed-loop — verify every screen (not a blind macro).** Before issuing a
324	  step's inputs, confirm the observer reports the expected screen; after issuing
325	  them, confirm the expected destination before proceeding. On mismatch, recover
326	  (see below) and re-plan. Never fire a button sequence open-loop and *assume* we
327	  landed where we hoped — drift, sticky defaults, variable/absent screens, and
328	  load times all break that. This is why the observer (M9) gates the controller
329	  (M10). (spec §4.8.1.)
330	- **Stubs / unknown destinations.** Edges marked `TBD` simply have no plan; the
331	  navigator never routes through them. Out-of-scope nodes (`tutorials_menu`) and
332	  any screen the observer doesn't recognize are treated as "unknown state."
333	- **Recovery from unknown state.** RED backs up one level from any menu, so the
334	  generic recovery is *"press RED until a recognized screen appears, then
335	  re-plan."* This gets us un-stuck from a wrong branch without mapping it.
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 18:53:14Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-15 18:53:25Z)**_

You remembered right, and the spec backs it — §4.8.1 explicitly says recognition is "bootstrapped offline: … prototyped host-side in Python against [the] corpus, and only the proven, simple GH3-specific logic is then ported into the firmware `gameplay_engine` module" (with Q10 favoring fixed-region/color/glyph matching over general CV). So: **offline Python first.**

Why that's clearly the right order, not just the documented one:

1. **It's the only one I can actually build *and* test here.** The corpus is committed and labeled (the filenames *are* ground truth); the uv env is available. Firmware navigation can't be compiled or hardware-tested in this environment, so open-loop firmware now would be untested, throwaway code.
2. **Closed-loop is the design we just enshrined.** The controller wants the observer to verify each screen. Build the observer first and the controller can be closed-loop from day one — open-loop-first would be a deliberate detour we'd then throw away.
3. **Open-loop buys little.** The forward training path is deterministic and already uses only fret/strum + green/red (no `+` needed until pause), so there's not much to "discover" by running it blind — and what little there is (sticky defaults, `part_select` absence) is exactly what needs the observer.

One scoping clarification: "all offline in Python" should cover **both** halves of §4.8 — the **observer** (screen classifier → then the region readers) **and** the **navigator/planner** (screen → next input). Offline we can't actuate, but we can run the whole thing as a *closed-loop sim* against the corpus: feed it a screen image, check it classifies correctly and picks the right next input along the graph. Then port the proven logic to firmware.

**Concrete first slice: the screen classifier.** Per Q10, per-screen fixed-region fingerprints rather than general CV — and we already have 101 labeled screens to validate against.

This is non-trivial and has real design choices (where the tool lives, fingerprint approach, how it consumes `gh3_navigation.md` as the graph, the sim harness shape), so I'd want to **plan it before coding**. Want me to enter plan mode and work up the offline game-state prototype (starting with the classifier)?
